s.g: An ethnic group in China, living mainly in a mountainous region in the northwestern part of Sichuan on the eastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau.
(historical) Any of various groups of people at different periods in ancient China, generally thought to have been of Tibetan-Burmese origin.
(Islam) The direction in which Muslims face while praying, currently determined as the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca.

qic.f: (computing) Initialism of quarter-inch cartridge: a tape storage format having a dual spooled cartridge with a quarter-inch wide tape.

qid.f: (Wikimedia jargon) Initialism of Q-identifier, a unique identifier for an item in Wikidata.

s.g: (fitness, alternative medicine) A Chinese system of breathing control, physical exercise and meditation.
A mythical Chinese hooved chimerical creature, said to appear in conjunction with the arrival of a sage.
(music) Any of several traditional Chinese musical instruments, most commonly the seven-stringed instrument more specifically called the guqin.
A sounding stone, a Chinese musical instrument.
A traditional one-piece dress worn by Chinese women.
A former currency of Iran (from 1825 to 1932), subdivided into 20 shahi or 1000 dinar and worth one tenth of a toman.
(Islam, law) Under sharia law, the principle of retaliation in kind, or retributive justice.
A member of the Turkmen tribes who formed the basis of the military power of the Safavids.
